title: Multiple Claude accounts
summary: Keeps multiple Claude accounts signed in on the same PC, with no signing out and in. It sets up two: "claude" and "claude -P".
benefit: You use your Claude accounts side by side on one PC, with one setup.
solves: Signing out and in again every time you switch between Claude accounts on the same PC.
use_cases: "claude" opens one account and "claude -P" the other, both signed in at the same time.
Any two accounts, for example work and personal. You choose their labels and the flag.
Settings, skills, hooks, plugins and sessions are shared; login, plan and usage limits stay separate.
Change the setup once in ~/.claude: a sync runs before every start of the second account.
Resuming a session started under the other account works, and uses the current account's limits.
This part sets up two accounts; three or more are not supported yet.
Other shells such as cmd.exe and IDE extensions open the main account only.
details: claude opens one account and claude -P the other, both signed in at once: a shell function in your shell profiles points the second start at a second config folder you choose, and a sync script refreshes junctions so settings, skills, hooks and sessions are shared while login, plan and usage limits stay separate. Use it when you have two Claude logins. It edits your shell profiles, creates junctions in the config folder and adds a skill with the sync steps, loaded only when used; no network.
trigger: Type claude -P (or your chosen flag) to start the second account.

values.ask: Label of the account logged in under ~/.claude (for example Work)
Label of the second account (for example Personal)
Login email of the second account
Shell flag that opens the second account (default -P; must not be a real Claude Code flag)
Config folder name of the second account, with the dot

user_steps: In a new terminal run "claude -P" (or your flag), run /login and sign in with the other account, then accept the folder trust prompt and check /status shows the other email.
machine_steps: Replace {{SECOND_DIR}} in the merged session-start hook entry in settings.json with the second folder name chosen above.

Insert wrapper.bash from ~/.claude/tools/two-accounts/ as a block into ~/.bashrc (replace an old block between "# >>> claude accounts >>>" and "# <<< claude accounts <<<"). Check that bash -lic "type -t claude" prints function; if not, add a line that sources ~/.bashrc to the login profile.
Insert wrapper.ps1 the same way into the PowerShell profile $PROFILE.CurrentUserAllHosts, once for each PowerShell the person uses. Check that (Get-Command claude).CommandType prints Function.
Run node ~/.claude/tools/sync-second-profile.mjs --profile-dir <second folder> once. It creates the second folder and links the shared folders into it as junctions.
If the status line is installed, set ACCT2_MATCH and ACCT2_LABEL in ~/.claude/statusline.sh to the second account email and label.
If the sync warns that the claude executable is not found, set the user environment variable CLAUDE_ACCOUNTS_CLAUDE_BIN to the full path of claude.exe (never claude.cmd).
risk: Edits shell profile files, creates junctions into the Claude config folder, and runs a sync before each second-profile start; no network.
